architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

planner.failure_mode: isothermal viscosity growth during prolonged residence at 120 C, with insufficiently resolved attribution to reactive-core dilution versus modifier-specific stabilization
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal-hold measurements show a 15-to-60 min relative viscosity change of 9.51% for E1 but 51.54% for E5, with the E5 trajectory reaching 93.08% by 90 min.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have original thermal-hold data, each from a single run with four points over 15 to 90 min. The local data therefore establish a large endpoint contrast but do not resolve repeatability, intermediate-time trajectory shape, or whether drift suppression depends on the acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like axes. By comparison, temperature response has six-point sweeps across 80 to 130 C for multiple runs, while realized viscosity level is quantified at several temperatures for E2, despite substantial spread.
measurement_requirements: Use a matched-window 120 C thermal hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and at least two independent repeats.
Compare a reactive-core-only or acrylic-only composition with a composition containing a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction at comparable reactive mass fraction.
Report the 15-to-60 min relative change for each repeat and compare it with the frozen linear-dilution prediction from E1.
Record the initial realized viscosity level and preparation history so viscosity-scale displacement is not conflated with isothermal drift.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched measurement window, does a resin-modified composition suppress 120 C viscosity drift beyond the linear dilution prediction, and is that suppression obtained only when the minor tackifier-like axis is nonzero rather than from the acrylic-like axis alone?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-DUAL: a dual-axis card can show that the combined intervention suppresses drift, but cannot establish that the minor-tackifier axis is required without a matched acrylic-only comparator.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If matched-window drift is below half the linear-dilution prediction, approximately below 3.80% because the reactive mass fraction is 0.80, this supports H-RESIN and rejects reactive-core-only dilution as an adequate explanation. The result also demonstrates strong stabilization for a composition using both independently supported modifier axes, but does not by itself prove tackifier necessity.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If drift remains at or above the linear-dilution prediction, approximately 7.61%, the result supports H-CORE relative to this intervention and falsifies the predicted superlinear suppression of H-RESIN; it also challenges the H-DUAL prediction for low drift when the tackifier axis is active.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between approximately 3.80% and 7.61% indicates some suppression relative to dilution but is insufficient to support H-RESIN's pre-registered superlinear criterion. It would leave the mechanism unresolved and motivate a matched acrylic-only comparison to test H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only composition directly probes acrylic-axis behavior and is inside the supported region, but it cannot test the performance of the combined intervention and its high-drift outcome would leave H-CORE and H-DUAL difficult to distinguish.
The 5% minor-tackifier-only composition is well supported and is useful for axis attribution, but it omits the acrylic-like axis needed for the intended performance-mitigation intervention.
Repeatability control addresses the large realization-state spread but does not directly measure the declared failure mode, thermal-hold drift.

proposer.reasoning: S1C41 uses 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier, both within externally supported intervention regions, while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions and retaining 80% reactive mass. The matched 120 C hold directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate with no model-fit inference and at least two independent repeats. Its linear-dilution benchmark is 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61%, while H-RESIN predicts less than half that value. The card therefore provides a direct and interpretable test of whether a supported dual-axis intervention suppresses drift beyond dilution, while its limitation regarding tackifier necessity is explicitly retained.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Prefer the reactive-core-only matched-hold control represented by S1C05 before S1C41, to establish an E2-core drift benchmark using the identical repeat protocol and avoid attributing core effects to resin modification.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Deterministic ranking and tied top set are withheld, so membership cannot be established. The proposal is scientifically motivated as a dual-axis performance-mitigation hold, but it should not be treated as validated against a deterministic VOI ranking.
residual_decision_risk: The payload does not explicitly map S1C05 to the E2 composition, so candidate identity should be verified before execution.
The proposed dual-axis intervention remains unable to establish whether the minor-tackifier axis is required without a matched acrylic-only comparator.
Repeat aggregation and uncertainty relative to the benchmark must be prespecified.
Large realization-state variability may obscure formulation effects even with repeated holds.
Matched-window drift supports formulation-level rheological hypotheses but not a molecular reaction pathway.
VOI stability metrics were withheld, so sensitivity to weighting cannot be quantified.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is substantive rather than interpretive: S1C41 uses E1's 9.51% drift as its linear-dilution benchmark even though it preserves the different E2 reactive core. A result from S1C41 therefore cannot cleanly distinguish modifier-specific suppression from reactive-core or stoichiometric effects. A matched unmodified E2-core M-HOLD-120 experiment should be run first or as the required control, with the drift coefficient frozen before interpreting S1C41. The objection also leaves H-DUAL unresolved because S1C41 activates both modifier axes.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No recommendation_flip_boundary, top_experiment_set_stability, or base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is supplied; therefore no defensible weight perturbation analysis is possible. The decision should instead be governed by the unmatched reactive-core benchmark identified by the Skeptic.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The criterion of drift at or above approximately 7.61% is based on the directly measured SI_15_60 from the 120 C hold, so the protocol can produce the required result without fitting or extrapolation. Its scientific interpretation is weakened because the 7.61% benchmark is not based on a matched E2 reactive-core reference, and the proposal lacks a prespecified replicate aggregation rule.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low drift result could support combined-intervention performance and phenomenological superlinear suppression, but it could not establish that the minor tackifier is required or attribute the suppression to either modifier axis.
objections.objection: The proposed S1C41::M-HOLD-120 separates H-CORE from H-RESIN only through the benchmark 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61% and the H-RESIN threshold of 3.80%. Those predictions are separated by 3.81 percentage points, which exceeds the declared 2.0% resolution, so the numerical separation itself is adequate. However, H-DUAL remains entangled because S1C41 simultaneously activates the 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like axes; the proposer correctly declares that a matched acrylic-only comparator is absent.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment cannot cleanly reject reactive-core or stoichiometric explanations; an apparent deviation from 7.61% may reflect the E1-to-E2 core difference rather than resin-specific stabilization.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes at once (15% acrylic-like plus 5% minor tackifier-like), while also reducing reactive mass to phi_r = 0.80. Therefore any drift change is compatible with acrylic action, tackifier action, an interaction, or dilution. More importantly, the linear benchmark is taken from E1, whose original core has NCO:OH = 1.70 and 80.713% polyol fraction, whereas S1C41 preserves the E2 core proportions and is based on the E2 center with NCO:OH = 1.80. The E1 thermal-hold coefficient is therefore not a clean matched reactive-core coefficient for S1C41.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No major interpretability problem follows for the matched-window drift claim; the limitation is attribution, not the readout itself.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly calculated from viscosity readings at 15 and 60 minutes in M-HOLD-120. It requires no model fit, extrapolation, or imputation, and the 3.80% versus 7.61% decision boundaries are farther apart than the declared 2.0% resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A borderline result could be classified as supporting H-CORE or falsifying H-RESIN without a reproducible rule for handling between-repeat variation.
objections.objection: The stated falsification result for H-RESIN, drift at or above 7.61%, is measurable directly with M-HOLD-120, so the criterion is attainable in principle. However, the protocol specifies only 'at least two independent repeats' and does not define how repeat results will be combined or how uncertainty will be compared with the 7.61% boundary. The catalog's 2.0% resolution is declared for the repeat protocol, but the proposal does not specify a prespecified replicate-level decision rule.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could be overinterpreted as proof of a particular concentration or encounter-frequency mechanism rather than evidence for the registered phenomenological H-RESIN prediction.
objections.objection: The proposal does not appear to use validation-formulation identity, wet-lab outcome, or outcome-derived labels, so there is no clear result leakage. However, the statement that resin modification suppresses drift by 'lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species within a non-reactive continuum' is not established by the planned rheological hold. M-HOLD-120 can adjudicate a formulation-level drift pattern, not that specific physical mechanism.

skeptic.recommended_change: Use a matched E2 reactive-core baseline, or measure the unmodified E2 core with the identical M-HOLD-120 repeat protocol and freeze its drift coefficient before testing S1C41. To test H-DUAL, add a matched acrylic-only composition at the same reactive mass fraction, alongside the dual-axis composition and the reactive-core control, with the same 120 C hold and at least two independent preparations per composition.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The linear-dilution benchmark uses E1's 9.51% drift even though the proposed S1C41 composition preserves the materially different E2 reactive core (including NCO:OH = 1.80 versus E1's 1.70). Because the baseline coefficient is not matched to the proposed core, failure to meet 7.61% cannot uniquely distinguish resin-specific suppression from core stoichiometry or core-composition effects.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity from 80 to 130 C in 10 C increments on a freshly prepared sample and regress ln(eta) against 1/T.

measurement_plan.name: one-point state calibration check
measurement_plan.primary_observable: multiplicative reconstruction error of the 120-130 C response from a single 110 C anchor
measurement_plan.protocol: Measure viscosity at 110 C only, locate the realization on the shared local thermal response, then verify the predicted 120 and 130 C values against direct measurement.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.

measurement_plan.name: repeatability / state-control experiment
measurement_plan.primary_observable: between-preparation spread of the realized viscosity-scale coordinate a_fr at matched temperature
measurement_plan.protocol: Prepare the same nominal composition three times under a controlled and fully recorded process history, then measure the 80-130 C sweep for each preparation.
